meta.title: Operation of Microscope with Camera Attachment in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To capture high-resolution photomicrographs of plant tissue sections, pollen grains, trichomes, and cellular structures for documentation, publication, herbarium records, and teaching in Pharmacognosy.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for digital photodocumentation of microscopic drug characteristics, authentication records, and preparation of teaching materials.
procedure: Mount the digital camera or C-mount camera adapter securely on the trinocular or camera port of the microscope.
Connect the camera to the PC/laptop via USB cable or wireless connection.
Open the camera imaging software on the PC and verify the camera is detected and live preview is visible.
Switch on the microscope illumination and set the light path to the camera port using the trinocular prism switch.
Prepare the slide and locate the structure of interest using the eyepieces (10× objective first).
Switch the live view to the camera preview on the monitor.
Optimize illumination for imaging: use Köhler illumination if available; adjust condenser aperture for best contrast.
Focus precisely using the fine focus knob — use live preview zoom-in feature if the software supports it.
Adjust white balance in the software using a blank field (empty slide area under same illumination).
Set appropriate exposure settings — use auto-exposure as starting point then adjust manually to avoid over/under exposure.
Navigate the slide to the structure to be photographed.
Capture the image using the software capture button (avoid touching the microscope during capture to prevent motion blur).
Add calibration scale bar using the software's scale bar tool — calibrate using a stage micrometer slide.
Save images with systematic file names: DrugName_Structure_Magnification_Date (e.g., Neem_Leaf_TS_40x_2026-07-12).
Print or export annotated images for records and laboratory practical files.
Clean the camera port and cover after use; store the camera in its case.
Log all imaging sessions in the equipment register.
precautions: Ensure the camera adapter is securely fastened to the trinocular port before use — a dropped camera is a catastrophic loss.
Never exceed the rated camera weight on the trinocular port — heavy cameras require a separate support stand.
Calibrate the scale bar using a certified stage micrometer slide — uncalibrated scale bars in publications are a serious scientific error.
Protect the camera sensor from direct illumination without a specimen in place — bright direct light can permanently damage camera sensors.
Use a remote shutter release or software trigger to avoid camera shake during image capture.
Back up all photomicrographic images immediately to a networked or cloud storage location.
Do not use cleaning solvents directly on the camera body or lens — use only lens paper and approved lens cleaner.
